title.narrative: Improved national social protection system in Rwanda

description.narrative:
Rwanda’s National Strategy for Transformation (NST1) highlights the central role of social protection in poverty reduction and improving the standard of living for all citizens. The "Reinforcing Social Security System and Implementation of National Policies" initiative aims to enhance Rwanda's social protection system, with a particular focus on expanding coverage for informal workers and strengthening the linkages between social protection and employment.
The project supports the Government of Rwanda in strengthening both contributory and non-contributory social protection schemes, such as the Rwanda Social Security Board's (RSSB) pension and health schemes, and the national social assistance program (VUP) for vulnerable households. Despite significant progress, coverage remains limited, with contributory schemes reaching less than 10% of the population. The COVID-19 pandemic further underscored the vulnerability of workers, particularly those in informal employment, which constitutes 87% of the workforce.
This project seeks to increase social protection coverage through targeted interventions that will expand access to pensions, maternity leave, and unemployment benefits, especially for informal workers. Additionally, it aims to improve the operational capacity of the Rwanda Social Security Board and the Ministry of Public Service and Labour (MIFOTRA), and enhance compliance with social protection schemes. The initiative also includes evidence-based advocacy to strengthen public understanding of a life-cycle, rights-based approach to social protection and to ensure sustainable financing for the system.
The project is aligned with Rwanda’s broader development goals, including achieving universal social protection and advancing gender equality. It is supported by the ILO’s Global Flagship Programme on Building Social Protection Floors for All, and will contribute to Rwanda's participation in the Global Accelerator on Jobs and Social Protection for Just Tran
